I've ported the word counter to Go, and all 6 example cases pass with `node check.mjs`.

I also checked it against the original Node program on a 50 MB generated file and a 3 MB file of random bytes. The output was identical both times, and the Go version took about 0.16s on the 50 MB file versus 0.82s for Node. Unit tests for the spec rules and for words split across read chunks also pass with `go test ./...`.
